# The Narrator

Unnamed (Q-0002). The voice that opens and closes every episode — and the proof,
standing centuries downstream, that the world survived.

## Role

> status: ratified (D-0035, D-0036, D-0047)

A religious scholar of the history of the study of the Wyrd and Frith, of an order
generations deep in real understanding ([[religion]]). Probably omniscient in
narrative function; certainly not a character inside the events. They own the cold
open and the outro, intruding between only as needed. Their perspective is
centuries-out; their materials are songs, poems, tapestries, and history quotes; and
they carry a very oblique sense that a better future followed this story — without
ever being explicit about their own present, which is far removed from the events.

## The manuscript at a remove

> status: ratified (D-0038, D-0045)

The Handmaid's-Tale trick: what we hear is drawn from records far removed in time
from the events. The narrator quotes — with clear historical remove — rather than
merely speaks: apocryphal legends, registers of woven chronicles, fragments of
outlawed poetry ([[in-world-texts]], [[narrator-framing]]).

## Identity and era

> status: ratified (D-0104, D-0117)

The narrator is heir to the criminalized skalds — the memory-keepers whose reciting was a
capital offence in story-time — who, centuries on, have become the scholarly order of the
study of Wyrd and Frith (D-0047). The hunted reciters won: memory outlasts the empire's
memory-policing, and that vindication is the frame's quiet hope. The narrator's own era
stays abstract and carries no live tension (D-0104); what is revealed is only that someone
survived to study this, and studies it with reverence. The order takes its name from that
skald root — the proper name is still unfixed (Q-0002), the illustrative "Skaldmoot" having
passed the oracle.

## Proposed texture

> status: proposed

Unratified: a "thread-reader" of a bog-archive monastery in the lowlands, translating the
great woven chronicle of the trio's era; a voice of Le-Guin/Clarke warmth and dryness (voice
models provisional under D-0083); the sound of a loom or turning card stock under the
opening lines. One optional late reveal held in reserve: the order's oldest "source" is the
still-living moor-hound (D-0116), and a scholar who reads the hound is reading a living
witness of the trio — kept always as the order's source, never the narrator itself.

## Naming policy: placeholder, not a project

> status: ratified (D-0130)

The narrator may never speak his own name in-show, and his naming is closed as a
design project (D-0130: "just give it a placeholder and move on. a backstory, yes,
but the naming is a rabbit hole"). Working placeholder: **Webster**. Alternates on
record from the author's review: Limner, and Fennon — his pick as the best of the
place-derived personal names, banked for reuse. Backstory development continues;
name development does not. The ORDER's proper name is closed the same way (D-0149:
"stop digging") — the narrator is functionally omniscient and will not talk about
himself, so "Skaldmoot" stays illustrative-only, indefinitely.
